aiAgents.mandateActiveHint:
Trade one side for realized profit.
• Opens only when it sees a setup with edge — stays flat on hostile tape, never robotically re-enters after a stop
• Places both a stop-loss and a take-profit on every position
• Manages open trades: adds to winners, trims into strength, moves stops to breakeven, cuts broken theses
• Success = realized P&L per trade
aiAgents.mandateAccumulateHint:
Build long exposure patiently.
• Buys only weakness: flushes, panics, oversold dips — never chases strength, and may stay flat if direction edge is not clear
• Places a stop-loss but NO automatic take-profit — winners are never auto-clipped; you decide when the campaign ends
• Adds (DCA) on further dips while the thesis holds; trims only at euphoric extremes or if the thesis decays
• Success = better average entry
aiAgents.mandateAccumulateShortHint:
Build short exposure patiently.
• Shorts only strength: euphoric rallies, overbought spikes into resistance — never chases breakdowns, and may stay flat if direction edge is not clear
• Places a stop-loss but NO automatic take-profit — the position is never auto-covered; you decide when the campaign ends
• Adds on further strength while the thesis holds; covers partially only at capitulation extremes or if the thesis decays
• Success = better average short entry

trading.orderTypesDescription:
Market: fills immediately at the best available price.

Limit: fills only at your limit price or better.

Stop Market: triggers a market order when the trigger price is reached (longs: trigger above mid, shorts: below). Used for breakout entries or stop-loss exits.

Stop Limit: triggers a limit order at your limit price once the trigger fires (longs: trigger above mid, shorts: below). Same direction as Stop Market, with a price cap to control slippage.

Take Market: triggers a market order when the trigger price is reached (longs: trigger below mid, shorts: above). Used for buy-the-dip / sell-the-rip entries or take-profit exits.

Take Limit: triggers a limit order at your limit price once the trigger fires (longs: trigger below mid, shorts: above). Same direction as Take Market, with a price cap to control slippage.
trading.marginModesDescription:
Isolated: Margin & Pnl are not shared between positions. You will only lose the current position if liquidation occurs.

Cross: Margin & Pnl are shared across all positions. You may lose all your positions if liquidation occurs.

whatIsHyperTrade.question: What is HyperTrade?
whatIsHyperTrade.answer: HyperTrade is a blockchain-based interface that lets you trade spot and perpetual futures on stocks, crypto, commodities, and forex. To complete the circle, we now offer a Swiss-licensed IBAN with multi-currency support and a free Mastercard, giving you a direct bridge from your wallet to everyday payments worldwide.

differentFromBrokers.question: How is HyperTrade different from traditional brokers?
differentFromBrokers.answer: Traditional brokers hold your funds in their accounts and execute trades on their systems. HyperTrade is non-custodial: your funds stay in your wallet on the blockchain, and trades are settled directly on-chain 24/7. This means you have full ownership and control, with no intermediary holding your assets.

airdropAndToken.question: Will there be a HyperTrade airdrop?
airdropAndToken.answer:
While we firmly believe in rewarding early users, we have decided to postpone token & airdrop until the global regulatory landscape around crypto improves. We want any distribution to be compliant, durable, and fair to users — not rushed into legal uncertainty.

When it happens, our planned design allocates over 50% of the total LWL supply to the airdrop. This is not a marketing gimmick; it reflects our conviction that HyperTrade should be owned by its users, not insiders.

Why >50%? HyperTrade is currently self-funded, and we do not plan to onboard VCs whose interests might dilute user rewards. Even if we eventually partner with strategic investors, we are committed to keeping the community allocation above 50% — because the airdrop’s purpose is to reward actual HyperTrade usage, not passive speculation.

Following Hyperliquid’s footsteps — we deeply admire how Hyperliquid turned its users into co-founders. Our goal is the same: every meaningful LWL holder should be a power user who contributed to the app’s growth. The airdrop will be structured around on-chain activity, volume, loyalty, and feature engagement — not just snapshot farming.

What you can do now — use HyperTrade consistently. The best way to maximize a future claim is to become an authentic, active participant in the app today. When the regulatory environment is ready, we will announce the airdrop with ample lead time and full transparency.

whatArePerps.question: What are perpetual futures (perps)?
whatArePerps.answer: Perpetual futures are derivative contracts that let you trade the price of an asset (like stocks, crypto, or commodities) without owning it. Unlike regular futures, perps don't have an expiration date—you can hold them as long as you want. You can go "long" (betting the price goes up) or "short" (betting the price goes down).

whatIsLeverage.question: What is leverage?
whatIsLeverage.answer: Leverage lets you control a larger position with less capital. For example, with 10x leverage, you can open a $1,000 position using only $100 of your own money. While leverage amplifies profits, it also amplifies losses. If your position moves against you, you can lose more than your initial deposit. Always use leverage carefully and understand the risks.

whatIsMargin.question: What is margin?
whatIsMargin.answer: Margin is the collateral you need to open and maintain a leveraged position. It's the amount of funds you must have in your account to keep your trade open. If your position loses value and your margin falls below the required level, your position may be liquidated (closed automatically) to prevent further losses.

whatIsFundingRate.question: What is a funding rate?
whatIsFundingRate.answer: Funding rates are periodic payments exchanged between long and short traders. If the funding rate is positive, longs pay shorts; if negative, shorts pay longs. Rates typically update every 8 hours and help keep the perpetual contract price aligned with the underlying asset's spot price. You'll see funding fees deducted or added to your account automatically.

orderTypes.question: What order types are available?
orderTypes.answer:
• Market Order: Executes immediately at the current market price.
• Limit Order: Executes only when the price reaches your specified level.
• Stop Loss: Automatically closes your position if the price moves against you to limit losses.
• Take Profit: Automatically closes your position when it reaches a profitable price level.

freeWallet.question: Does HyperTrade create a free wallet for me?
freeWallet.answer: Yes! HyperTrade includes a free wallet that's automatically created when you sign up. This wallet lets you deposit funds, withdraw to external wallets, and execute trades with one tap. You have full control over your wallet custody and actions.

howToDeposit.question: How do I deposit USDC?
howToDeposit.answer: Go to your Profile and tap "Deposit", you can deposit USDC (USD Coin) directly to the provided wallet address. Alternatively, you can buy USDC with a credit or debit card via Moonpay (requires KYC).

whatIsArbitrumUsdc.question: What is Arbitrum USDC?
whatIsArbitrumUsdc.answer: USDC is a digital dollar that lives on many blockchains like Ethereum & Solana. In our app, Arbitrum blockchain is used for USDC deposits and withdrawals.

withdrawToExternal.question: Can I withdraw my USDC to external wallet like MetaMask or Binance?
withdrawToExternal.answer: Yes! Navigate to Profile → "Settings" → "Withdraw USDC". Enter the destination wallet address and the amount you want to withdraw. Withdrawals are processed on-chain and typically complete in 1-3 minutes.

whyMoveFunds.question: Why do i need to move funds between wallet balance and trade balance?
whyMoveFunds.answer: We use a two-balance system to improve security, prevent spam & enable features like one-tap trading.

withdrawDifference.question: What is the difference between withdrawing USDC back to wallet balance and external wallet?
withdrawDifference.answer: When you withdraw USDC back to your wallet balance, it means the USDC lives in the wallet balance we created for you. When you withdraw USDC to an external wallet, it means the USDC will be transferred to the external wallet address you provided outside HyperTrade e.g. your personal MetaMask or Binance wallet.

howToExportWallet.answer: You can export your private keys from https://home.privy.io. Use the same login method you used on HyperTrade. Privy is a trusted third-party wallet provider that we use to create your wallet.

oneTapTrading.question: How does 1-tap trading work?
oneTapTrading.answer: With the free wallet HyperTrade created for you, your wallet is pre-connected with valid authorization, so you don't need to approve each transaction separately. This makes trading fast and seamless, especially for active traders.

perpsSpotFree.question: Is moving USDC between perps and spot balances free?
perpsSpotFree.answer: Yes! Moving USDC between perps and spot balances is free.

minimumAmount.question: What is the minimum amount I can execute a trade with?
minimumAmount.answer: The minimum amount you can execute a trade with is $10. You might need to clamp the amount a bit higher to avoid rounding and price changes errors.

spotAssets.question: What assets are available for spot trading?
spotAssets.answer: At the moment, only BTC, ETH, SOL & HYPE are available for spot trading.

noTpslSpot.question: Why is there no TP/SL for spot trading?
noTpslSpot.answer: We are working on adding TP/SL for spot trading, it will be available soon.

liquidation.question: What happens if my perps position gets liquidated?
liquidation.answer: If the position was opened with Isolated margin, only that position will be liquidated and you'll lose the margin you used to open the position. In a cross-margin setup, a single liquidation can potentially wipe out your entire available margin for perpetual trading.

spotLiquidation.question: How does perpetual liquidation work with my trade balance?
spotLiquidation.answer: Liquidation closes a perpetual position when its margin is insufficient. With a unified trade balance, collateral and liquidation prices are shown in one place—watch the liquidation price in the app and manage position size and risk accordingly.

tradingFeesCalculated.question: How are trading fees calculated?
tradingFeesCalculated.answer: Trading fees are clearly displayed before you execute a trade. Fees are typically a small percentage of your trade size and vary based on the asset and whether you are maker or taker.

fundingRatePurpose.question: What is the purpose of funding rate?
fundingRatePurpose.answer: Funding rates are periodic payments exchanged between long and short traders. If the funding rate is positive, longs pay shorts; if negative, shorts pay longs. Rates help keep the perpetual contract price aligned with the underlying asset's spot price.

fundingRateGain.question: Can my live perps position gain from funding rate?
fundingRateGain.answer: Yes! Your live position can gain from funding rate if the funding rate is negative and you are long or if the funding rate is positive and you are short. Funding rates are displayed clearly in the relative asset page.

reduceExposure.question: How can I reduce exposure to a live perps position?
reduceExposure.answer: You can reduce exposure by partially closing your position with a reduce only order. If you are long, you can partially short your position (or vice versa) as long as you have enough margin to cover the new position.

multipleAssets.question: Can I trade multiple assets at once?
multipleAssets.answer: Yes! You can open multiple positions across different assets simultaneously. Each position is independent, so you can be long on one asset and short on another. Just make sure you have enough margin to cover all your open positions.

tradingHistory.question: Can I see my trading history?
tradingHistory.answer: Yes! Navigate to Profile → "Trade History" to see all your past trades, positions, and P&L (profit and loss) records. You can also view your deposit and withdrawal history in Profile → "Deposit & Withdraw History".

stocksForex.question: Are these equities, commodities and forex assets real?
stocksForex.answer: While you don't own the underlying asset, you can trade them just like you would trade crypto. We utilize third party services that allow us to list "Synthetic Perpetuals." These contracts track the price of non-crypto assets (like Nvidia or Gold) without requiring the underlying physical asset.

pricingWork.question: How does the pricing work for synthetic equities and forex?
pricingWork.answer: Accuracy is maintained via oracles e.g. Pyth, a premier institutional oracle. Oracles provide low-latency, high-frequency price feeds directly from global exchanges (like the NYSE or NASDAQ) and major banking institutions. This ensures that the "Mark Price" on your screen reflects the real-time global value of the asset with sub-second precision.

trading247.question: Is trading for stocks and forex 24/7?
trading247.answer: Yes! Unlike traditional brokers, these markets never close. When the underlying global markets (like the NYSE) are closed for weekends or holidays, the protocol enters an Internal Pricing Session. You can continue to trade 24/7, but the price is protected by "Discovery Bounds" to prevent irrational volatility while the primary oracle is offline.

discoveryBounds.question: What are "Discovery Bounds" and how do they protect me?
discoveryBounds.description: Discovery Bounds are leverage-based limits that restrict how far the price can move from the last official closing price.
discoveryBounds.ruleText: The price can only move within a range of 1 / Max Leverage.
discoveryBounds.benefitText: This ensures market participants can trade with confidence during the weekend without fear of "flash crashes" or artificial manipulation.
discoveryBounds.equities: • Equities (e.g., NVDA, TSLA): Max Leverage 10x, Range ±10% from close.
discoveryBounds.commodities: • Commodities (e.g., Gold, Oil): Max Leverage 20x, Range ±5% from close.
discoveryBounds.forex: • Forex (e.g., EUR, JPY): Max Leverage 50x, Range ±2% from close.

openInterestCap.question: Why do I get "Open Interest Cap" error when placing a trade on equities, commodities or forex?
openInterestCap.answer: Open Interest (OI) represents the total value of all open positions in a market. Each market has a dedicated OI cap to ensure market stability and liquidity. Once this cap is reached, new positions cannot be opened until open interest falls below the specified limit—only existing positions may be reduced or closed.
openInterestCap.stocks: • Popular stocks (e.g., TSLA, NVDA, GOOGL): Caps range from $50M-$100M
openInterestCap.commodities: • Commodities (e.g., GOLD, SILVER, COPPER): Caps range from $100M-$200M
openInterestCap.forex: • Forex pairs (e.g., EUR, JPY): Caps typically $25M
openInterestCap.note: These caps are subject to change and will likely increase over time as markets mature. For the most up-to-date OI cap information, visit the asset's detail page in the app.

fastLiquidation.question: What happens if the market moves too fast for a liquidation?
fastLiquidation.answer: In extreme market conditions (like a "black swan" event in a stock), if a trader's position cannot be closed in the open market before their margin runs out, the Insurance Fund steps in to cover the loss. This ensures that no user ever "owes" money to the platform; your maximum loss is always limited to your initial margin.

autoDeleveraging.question: What is "Auto-Deleveraging" (ADL) and how does it affect me?
autoDeleveraging.answer: If the Insurance Fund is unable to cover a massive liquidation, the protocol may trigger Auto-Deleveraging. This is a last-resort safety mechanism where the most profitable, highest-leveraged traders on the opposite side of a failing trade have their positions automatically closed at the "Bankruptcy Price."

whatIsDemo.answer:
Demo mode uses test network with virtual USDC. Trades and balances are for practice only — no real funds move and nothing settles to your real wallet.

aiAgentsFaq.title: AI Agents FAQ
aiAgentsFaq.notFound: This topic could not be found.

whatCanItDo.title: What can the agent do?
whatCanItDo.body:
Once live, your agent can open long or short positions on the asset you pick (one asset per agent), then manage them over time.

On open positions it can hold, add, trim, flip direction, or fully exit — including cutting losers early. It can also place stop-loss protection and tighten stops as a trade moves in your favor (it never loosens risk).

howDecisions.title: How does the AI make decisions?
howDecisions.body:
Each cycle the agent builds a market picture from live data — price action, open interest, liquidations, options, funding, and related flow signals — plus session/macro calendar context (time of day / macro events).

That context is sent to the AI model you chose. The model proposes an action; HyperTrade still enforces your rules (asset, leverage, notional caps) before any order is sent.

monitorCadence.title: How often does the agent check open positions?
monitorCadence.body:
All agents look for new entries about once an hour. How often an open trade is re-managed depends on the trading horizon:

• Scalper: about every hour
• Swing: about every hour
• Investor: about every 4 hours by default — mid-window checks are skipped unless risk fires (for example liquidation distance, near stop, earnings window, or a weakened thesis)

Between checks, exchange stop-loss orders still protect open positions.

sharedVsDedicated.title: Shared mode vs Dedicated?
sharedVsDedicated.body:
Shared mode (default): the agent trades from your main trade balance, limited by the notional caps you set (minimum $100). Best for getting started.

Dedicated: the agent gets its own separate balance — liquidations there don't hit your main trade balance. You can add or pull USDC back anytime with Transfer function found on the dedicated agent card. Unlocking Dedicated usually needs about $100k–$200k+ lifetime volume (closer to $100k if you've mostly traded crypto, higher if a lot of it is stocks).

You can easily switch between AI agents types and manage live/open orders in Trading Activity section.

switchingTradeAccount.title: Do my manual orders follow the selected agent?
switchingTradeAccount.body:
Yes. The Trade Account you pick is global — Home, Portfolio, and the trade screen all use the same selection, and it stays after you restart the app. It is not a view-only filter.

If you switch to a Dedicated agent (for example to check Trading Activity), any manual orders you place — including Quick Trade — go on that agent's book. Switch back to your main Trade Account when you want to trade with your main balance.

myMoney.title: Does it trade with my money?
myMoney.body:
Yes. In Shared mode the agent uses your main trade balance within the notional caps you set. In Dedicated mode it only uses USDC you moved into that agent's dedicated balance.

It signs orders with an agent key that you approve. That key can place trades but cannot withdraw funds from your account.

areAgentsFree.title: Are AI agents free to create?
areAgentsFree.body:
Yes — HyperTrade doesn't charge a fee to create or run an agent.

To activate one, the balance it trades from must hold at least $100 (main trade balance for Shared, or the agent's dedicated balance for Dedicated). Wallet USDC sitting outside Trade doesn't count until you move it over.

notionalBudget.title: How does max total notional work?
notionalBudget.body:
It's the agent's overall notional ceiling — a limit, not a target: the agent sizes by conviction and may use far less than the max. Combined open size still cannot exceed this total.

Minimum is $100 (Shared and Dedicated). Dedicated also asks for a separate funding amount (USDC moved into the dedicated balance at creation, also at least $100) — you can add or send back later from the agent card.

stayInControl.title: Do I stay in control?
stayInControl.body:
Yes. Agents start as drafts. You approve trading permission in your wallet, then activate when you're ready.

You can pause, stop, or revoke anytime. Stopping freezes new decisions; revoking also frees the agent's approval slot. Open positions stay yours to manage.

existingPosition.title: What if I already hold that coin?
existingPosition.body:
You can't assign a coin you already have an open position on. Close that position first, or pick a different asset for the agent.

This keeps the agent from sitting idle on a coin it can never open while you still hold it.

manualClose.title: What if I close an AI position myself?
manualClose.body: That's fine. On the next cycle the agent reconciles with reality — if you closed or reduced the position, it adopts that and won't force a re-open just to "fix" the book.

lossCooldown.title: Why won't the agent re-open after a losing trade?
lossCooldown.body:
After a loss-flavored close on a coin — for example a cut, stop hit, liquidation, or any exit that finished with negative realized PnL — the agent won't open a fresh position in that same coin for a cooldown period. This is a churn brake so it doesn't immediately re-enter and bleed fees.

Cooldown length depends on the agent's trading horizon:
• Scalper: about 1 hour
• Swing: about 1 hour
• Investor: about 2 hours

It only applies to that coin, not your whole agent. Winning exits (e.g. take-profit) don't start this cooldown. During the wait you may see a skipped cooldown decision in the agent's history — that's expected.

marginDust.title: Why did the agent close a tiny leftover position?
marginDust.body:
After trims, a position can shrink to a stub with very little margin left — too small to manage usefully, even if size still clears the exchange minimum.

On the next cycle, if that leftover margin is below a floor based on your max capital and trading horizon, the agent fully closes it as margin dust (no AI call). The same happens if a planned trim would leave a stub under that floor — it escalates to a full close instead.

The floor is at least $15 of margin, and scales with your budget:
• Scalper: max($15, 5% of max capital) — e.g. $50 on a $1k budget, $500 on $10k
• Swing / Investor: max($15, 3% of max capital) — e.g. $30 on $1k, $300 on $10k

Fresh small opens are left alone. This only sweeps reduced leftovers after the position has already been trimmed (or shrunk to about 40% of its opening size or less).

reasoning.title: Can I read the reasoning behind decisions?
reasoning.body:
Yes. On AI-managed positions in Portfolio, open Reasoning to see why the agent entered and its later check-ins.

You can also expand an agent on the AI Agents page to browse its recent decisions and summaries.

whichMarkets.title: Which markets can it trade?
whichMarkets.body:
Each agent trades exactly one market — pick the asset when you create it, and create a separate agent for each additional market you want covered.

Supported: crypto perpetuals (for example BTC, ETH, HYPE, SOL and other majors) plus select tokenized stock and commodity perpetuals where there is enough market data for autonomous trading. Assets without sufficient data can't be assigned.

howManyAgents.title: How many agents can I create?
howManyAgents.body:
Shared and Dedicated use separate limits.

• Shared: up to 2 agents per wallet (Hyperliquid named-agent room after the device wallet).
• Dedicated: up to 10 agents once unlocked (~$100k–$200k+ qualifying volume, crypto vs stocks) — one sub-account each, matching Hyperliquid’s base sub-account limit.

You can run both at once (for example 2 Shared + 10 Dedicated). Stopping an agent still holds its slot; revoke one you no longer need to free room for another.

agentSlots.title: What's the difference between stop and revoke?
agentSlots.body:
Stop pauses the agent — it won't make new decisions, but its trading approval stays active and still counts toward your agent limit. You can resume it later.

Revoke permanently disables the agent and removes its trading approval, freeing a slot so you can create or activate another. Open positions stay yours to manage.

whenThingsFail.title: What if data or the AI model is down?
whenThingsFail.body:
We don't close or auto-stop the agent on a bad cycle.

Open positions keep their exchange stops. If market data or the model is unavailable, the agent skips new decisions and retries next cycle. Sustained issues show a Needs attention warning (and a mobile notification if enabled) — you stay in control to pause, stop, or manage the position yourself.

risks.title: What are the risks?
risks.body:
Trading involves risk of loss. An AI agent can open losing trades, get stopped out, or underperform — the same as manual trading.

Set conservative caps, start small, and revoke anytime. This is not financial advice.

topUp.title: Top-up FAQ
topUp.body:
After verification, add money two ways:

Crypto (on-ramp): convert USDC (or other supported stablecoins) to fiat in your Cash balance. Any applicable fees are always shown transparently before you approve a transaction.

Bank transfer: send EUR or CHF via SEPA/SWIFT to your Swiss IBAN — from an account in your name; may take a few hours.

fees.title: Fees
fees.body:
HyperTrade adds no extra account or card fees.

Crypto ↔ cash (on-ramp and off-ramp): conversions between supported stablecoins and your Cash balance may include a fee from our fintech provider. Fees are always shown transparently before you approve a transaction.

Cash out to USDC (Withdraw in the Cash tab): a conversion fee plus a small network gas fee (typically < $0.1) may apply — all fees shown on the review screen before you confirm.

Card: paying in a different currency than the merchant bills may incur conversion fees — pay in the merchant's currency when you can.

Alipay: over ¥200 (~$25), Alipay charges 3% (not HyperTrade or our fintech provider).

Refunds: $1 per card refund.

Transfers — ~$100k monthly limit.

Pay-in (to your IBAN):
• EUR / CHF — min €1 or CHF 1, no max, free
• USD — min $1, no max, $5 per transfer

Payout (to external bank):
• EUR — min €1, max ~€107,767, free
• CHF — min CHF 1, max CHF 100,000, free
• USD — min $100, max $100,000, $50 per transfer

accountLimits.title: Account & card limits
accountLimits.body:
Your HyperTrade cash account has a rolling 30-day outbound limit of about $100,000 (USD equivalent). One shared cap covers all money moving out of your cash balances, including:

• Withdraw to USDC
• Convert between currencies
• Send to another HyperTrade user (P2P)
• Pay out to an external bank account
• Card spending

Your used amount counts down on a rolling 30-day basis — not a calendar month. The app shows how much you have left before you confirm a transfer.

Card spending has separate caps on top of the account limit:
• Daily: $10,000
• Monthly: $20,000

Both limits apply together — a large card purchase counts toward your account limit and your card caps.

iban.title: IBAN & bank transfers
iban.body:
After KYC you get a personal Swiss IBAN (USD, EUR, CHF & more) from our fintech provider.

SEPA & SWIFT — incoming transfers must be from accounts in your name.

Funds held are not covered by Swiss deposit protection (esisuisse).

cardFree.title: Is the card free?
cardFree.body: Yes — the HyperTrade virtual debit Mastercard is free to issue. There is no card subscription or shipping fee. It is a debit card, not credit — you spend from your cash account balance, not on borrowed funds.

cardSpendCurrency.title: Which currency does my card spend from?
cardSpendCurrency.body:
The paying currency is chosen per transaction in this order:

If the transaction currency is supported on HyperTrade (EUR, USD, CHF, GBP, CNH):
1. The matching transaction currency — e.g. EUR for a EUR merchant
2. USD
3. The currency with the highest balance

If the transaction currency is not supported on HyperTrade:
1. EUR
2. USD
3. The currency with the highest balance

physicalCard.title: Physical card & ATM withdrawals
physicalCard.body:
Today we issue a virtual debit Mastercard only — no plastic card is mailed yet, and ATM cash withdrawals are not available.

A physical card and ATM access are planned for a future release. ATM withdrawals will require a physical card on the same Mastercard network.

Your virtual card works like a physical card once added to a mobile wallet — contactless in stores plus online anywhere Mastercard is accepted.

Want a heads-up when physical cards and ATM withdrawals launch? Tap below while signed in and we'll notify you.

cardSpending.title: Using your HyperTrade card
cardSpending.body:
Your HyperTrade virtual debit Mastercard draws from your cash account balance with our fintech provider — not a credit line. Spend at millions of merchants online and in stores that accept your mobile wallet.

If you pay in a different currency than the merchant bills in, conversion fees may apply. Pay in the merchant's currency when you can.

mobileWallets.title: Mobile wallets & contactless pay
mobileWallets.body:
You can add your HyperTrade virtual card to Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, Alipay, WeChat Pay, and other supported wallets on your device — setup steps depend on the app and your region.

Once added, use contactless payments in stores and pay online anywhere your wallet and Mastercard are accepted. Complete any verification prompts from our fintech provider when you add the card.

withdrawals.title: Withdrawals & cash out
withdrawals.body:
Withdraw to USDC: move USD, EUR, or CHF from your cash balance back to USDC in your HyperTrade wallet. A conversion fee from our fintech provider plus a small network gas fee (typically < $0.1) may apply — all fees are always shown transparently before you approve a transaction.

Send to bank: pay out fiat to an external bank account via SEPA or SWIFT once fully verified. You authorize each transfer securely; timing depends on the rail and destination bank.

You can also top up via crypto (see Top-up FAQ), hold fiat in your cash accounts, convert between currencies in-app, then withdraw or send as needed.
